parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation exists, and civil society, Pride and pro-LGBTIQ health-ministry policy show embedded tolerance. However, the dossier documents tier-3 exposures: routine healthcare discrimination and scrutiny of trans women, a universal document/presentation mismatch with no legal gender recognition in operation, no anti-discrimination protection, unremedied prison-placement risk (solitary or general population only), and a 2025 government clampdown signal (Pride cancellations, surveillance of organisations, vague penal-code arrests). No visitor-specific border or police targeting is documented, and no trans-specific violence rate is quantifiable; the harshest documented harms are discrimination with thin recourse, not state prosecution of visitors. This sits between Elevated and Reduced: exposures are real but consequences fall below detention/custody severity.

entry_documents.exposure: Not addressed by any source; document-marker mismatch is a routine daily-life feature domestically, but border treatment of trans travellers is unknown.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown border screening could interact with the documented national ID-mismatch reality once inside.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: If detained, transgender prisoners can only be held in solitary or the general population; a 2015 proposal for separate housing had no enacted outcome; vague penal-code articles produced 43 arrests in 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any visitor encounter with police could escalate into custody with no gender-identity-matched placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prison and detention facilities lack gender-identity-matched housing; solitary or mixed placement is the documented only option.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Resident-facing gap, but operative for any visitor entering custody.

care_services.exposure: Routine discrimination at healthcare encounters for trans women — ID/presentation questioning, heightened scrutiny — plus stigma-driven risk of physical and sexual violence, concentrated among outlying provinces; implementing guidance for gender change stalled.
care_services.protection: 2022 health-ministry dispatch declares trans identity not an illness and bans forced conversion 'treatment'; free health care to citizens.
care_services.interaction: Visitors seeking care would face the same ID-verification friction documented for residents.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2002 ministry 'social evil' framing; organisations under government surveillance; 2025 Pride cancellations described as a clampdown; no anti-discrimination law on any ground.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Health ministry pro-LGBTIQ dispatch; Pride ran and expanded for over a decade; state broadcasts of events; growing public support.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State climate is deteriorating but enforcement against gender presentation specifically is not documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: No visitor-specific rule documented; resident data shows severe school bullying of trans students, a climate signal only.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion-practice ban since 2022 covers minors in principle.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Stigma-driven risk of physical and sexual violence for trans women, unquantified and without denominator; no trans-specific killing rate assessable.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police response to anti-trans violence not documented either way.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Visitors share the undocumented-recourse environment: no discrimination protection and thin formal remedies.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No legal gender recognition in operation; no SOGI discrimination protection; recourse for discrimination effectively absent; recognition law stalled since 2017 and still pending Feb 2026.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Draft recognition law under consideration; health-ministry dispatch; active LGBTIQ civil society.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A visitor cannot rely on any domestic remedy if outed and mistreated.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A: no traveller-facing register, exclusion mechanism, or universal state bar on entry exists; documented state exposures are discrimination and custody gaps, not systematic visitor exclusion.

Similar to 0.55-C: ward/service placement by documents, questioning at healthcare encounters, uneven facility practice, partial denial without custody threat or execution pathway. Here ID mismatch is even broader, but no criminal statute exists.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor has working remedies (tribunal, compensation, written reasons); this jurisdiction documents no discrimination protection, stalled recognition, no prison-placement remedy, and a 2025 clampdown signal.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is one of decriminalised, non-prosecuted gender diversity embedded in a society with real tolerance (Pride history, pro-LGBTIQ health policy, high youth support), but with no operative legal recognition, no anti-discrimination recourse, routine healthcare ID friction and stigma-driven violence risk, and custody placement that would expose any detained trans visitor to solitary or general-population housing. The 2025 clampdown raises outing-era severity modestly. No visitor-specific arrest, border, or prosecution pattern is documented, so the operative risk is discrimination and unremedied friction rather than state targeting — placing this at the top of Elevated Risk, around 0.58.
